text:
- **chief complaint:** Hospital follow-up after anterior STEMI treated with LAD drug-eluting stent; newly reduced ejection fraction (35%) and moderate mitral regurgitation.
- **history of present illness:** Prior CAD with RCA stent (2018) and hypertension and diabetes. Reports feeling mostly well since the STEMI, with mild walking and light housekeeping. Reports adherence to medications since discharge, and a low-salt diet has been discussed.
- **physical examination:** Vital signs stable. No jugular venous distention or carotid bruits. Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at left base, unchanged from last year. Lungs clear. No extremity edema. Right radial cath site clean, dry, and intact without hematoma; palpable radial pulse. ECG: normal sinus rhythm with expected post-MI changes.
- **symptoms experienced by the patient:** Occasional fatigue. No chest pain, shortness of breath, orthopnea (chronic two-pillow sleep), or leg swelling.
- **new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages:** Spironolactone (Aldactone) 12.5 mg daily (new).
- **follow-up instructions:** Labs next week. Repeat echocardiogram in about 2 months. Cardiac rehab referral. Continue aspirin 81 mg daily, ticagrelor (Brilinta) 90 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 80 mg daily, metoprolol succinate (Toprol) 50 mg daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. Monitor blood pressure at home. Reduce dietary salt.
